\chapter{If It Rains}
\label{ch:ml-if-it-rains}
\hlchaptermodality{347}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say what will happen if something happens, check a fact with -eṅkil, and give the other outcome with illeṅkil.}

Complete ML-R347-if-and-otherwise: real conditions with -āl and the future, -eṅkil on a full verb, and illeṅkil for \textquotedblleft{}otherwise\textquotedblright{}.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{നീ} \ml{വരുന്നുണ്ടെങ്കിൽ} (nī varunnuṇṭeṅkil)}{നീ വരുന്നുണ്ടെങ്കിൽ (nī varunnuṇṭeṅkil)}]{\ml{നീ} \ml{വരുന്നുണ്ടെങ്കിൽ} (nī varunnuṇṭeṅkil) — if you are coming}

\label{lesson:ML-C347-varunnundenkil}



\begin{quote}
Say \textquotedblleft{}if he comes\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{vannāl}.) Then the word that means \textquotedblleft{}if so, in that case\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{eṅkil}.)
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: a full verb, then \ml{എങ്കിൽ}}]
You already know \textbf{\ml{എങ്കിൽ}} on its own: \textquotedblleft{}if so\textquotedblright{}. Join it to a full verb and it says \textquotedblleft{}if it is so that …\textquotedblright{}:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ml{നീ} \ml{വരുന്നുണ്ടെങ്കിൽ} \ml{ഞാനും} \ml{വരാം}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nī varunnuṇṭeṅkil ñānuṁ varāṁ.} — \textquotedblleft{}If you are coming, I will come too.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\textbf{\ml{ഉണ്ട്}} gives \textbf{\ml{ഉണ്ടെങ്കിൽ}}, and \textbf{\ml{ആണ്}} gives \textbf{\ml{ആണെങ്കിൽ}}:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ml{സമയം} \ml{ഉണ്ടെങ്കിൽ} \ml{നമുക്ക്} \ml{സിനിമയ്ക്ക്} \ml{പോകാം}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{samayaṁ uṇṭeṅkil namukkŭ sinimaykkŭ pōkāṁ.} — \textquotedblleft{}If there is time, let us go to a film.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ml{അവൻ} \ml{വീട്ടിൽ} \ml{ആണെങ്കിൽ} \ml{ഞാൻ} \ml{വിളിക്കാം}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{avan vīṭṭil āṇeṅkil ñān viḷikkāṁ.} — \textquotedblleft{}If he is at home, I will call.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: \ml{ഇല്ലെങ്കിൽ}, otherwise}]
\textbf{\ml{ഇല്ല}} with \textbf{\ml{എങ്കിൽ}} is \textquotedblleft{}if not\textquotedblright{}, and at the head of a clause it is \textquotedblleft{}otherwise\textquotedblright{}:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ml{വേഗം} \ml{വരൂ}, \ml{ഇല്ലെങ്കിൽ} \ml{ബസ്} \ml{പോകും}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{vēgaṁ varū, illeṅkil basŭ pōkuṁ.} — \textquotedblleft{}Come quickly, otherwise the bus will go.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

So \textbf{\ml{ഇഷ്ടമില്ലെങ്കിൽ} \ml{വേണ്ട}}, \emph{iṣṭamilleṅkil vēṇṭa}, \textquotedblleft{}if you do not like it, leave it\textquotedblright{}.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textquotedblleft{}If you are coming, I will come too.\textquotedblright{}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}If there is time, let us go to a film.\textquotedblright{}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}If he is at home, I will call.\textquotedblright{}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}Come quickly, otherwise the bus will go.\textquotedblright{}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
\textquotedblleft{}If there is\textquotedblright{}? (\emph{\textbf{uṇṭeṅkil.}}) \textquotedblleft{}If it is\textquotedblright{}? (\emph{\textbf{āṇeṅkil.}}) \textquotedblleft{}Otherwise\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\ml{ഇല്ലെങ്കിൽ}}, \emph{illeṅkil}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{മഴ} \ml{പെയ്താൽ} (maḻa peytāl)}{മഴ പെയ്താൽ (maḻa peytāl)}]{\ml{മഴ} \ml{പെയ്താൽ} (maḻa peytāl) — if it rains}

\label{lesson:ML-C347-maza-peytal}



\begin{quote}
Say \textquotedblleft{}if he comes\textquotedblright{}, then \textquotedblleft{}tomorrow I will go\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{vannāl}; \emph{nāḷe ñān pōkuṁ}.) Then \textquotedblleft{}if you are coming\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{nī varunnuṇṭeṅkil}.)
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: -\ml{ആൽ}, then what will happen}]
A real condition is something that may well happen. Put \textbf{-\ml{ആൽ}} on the past form, as in \textbf{\ml{വന്നാൽ}}, and say what follows in the future, or with \textbf{-\ml{ആം}}, \textquotedblleft{}I will\textquotedblright{}:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ml{മഴ} \ml{പെയ്താൽ} \ml{ഞാൻ} \ml{വരില്ല}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{maḻa peytāl ñān varilla.} — \textquotedblleft{}If it rains, I will not come.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ml{നാളെ} \ml{സമയം} \ml{കിട്ടിയാൽ} \ml{ഞാൻ} \ml{വിളിക്കാം}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nāḷe samayaṁ kiṭṭiyāl ñān viḷikkāṁ.} — \textquotedblleft{}If I get time tomorrow, I will call.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

It also states what is true whenever the first thing happens:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ml{നേരത്തെ} \ml{ഉറങ്ങിയാൽ} \ml{രാവിലെ} \ml{ക്ഷീണം} \ml{തോന്നില്ല}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nēratte uṟaṅṅiyāl rāvile kṣīṇaṁ tōnnilla.} — \textquotedblleft{}If you sleep early, you do not feel tired in the morning.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

Roughly, \textbf{-\ml{ആൽ}} waits for an event, and \textbf{-\ml{എങ്കിൽ}} checks a fact: \emph{vannāl}, \textquotedblleft{}if he comes\textquotedblright{}; \emph{varunnuṇṭeṅkil}, \textquotedblleft{}if it is so that he is coming\textquotedblright{}.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: if it does not happen}]
For \textquotedblleft{}if … not\textquotedblright{}, put \textbf{-\ml{ഇല്ലെങ്കിൽ}} on the past form:

\begin{quote}
\textbf{\ml{നീ} \ml{വന്നില്ലെങ്കിൽ} \ml{ഞാൻ} \ml{വിളിക്കും}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nī vannilleṅkil ñān viḷikkuṁ.} — \textquotedblleft{}If you do not come, I will call.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textquotedblleft{}If it rains, I will not come.\textquotedblright{}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}If I get time tomorrow, I will call.\textquotedblright{}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}If you sleep early, you do not feel tired in the morning.\textquotedblright{}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}If you do not come, I will call.\textquotedblright{}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
\textquotedblleft{}If it rains\textquotedblright{}? (\emph{\textbf{maḻa peytāl.}}) \textquotedblleft{}If I get\textquotedblright{}? (\emph{\textbf{kiṭṭiyāl.}}) \textquotedblleft{}If you do not come\textquotedblright{}? (\emph{\textbf{nī vannilleṅkil.}})
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(review)]{Review — if, and otherwise}

\label{lesson:ML-R347-if-and-otherwise}



\begin{quote}
Write \textbf{\ml{ഋതു}} once from memory. Then say \textquotedblleft{}if it rains\textquotedblright{} and \textquotedblleft{}if you are coming\textquotedblright{}. (\emph{maḻa peytāl}, \emph{nī varunnuṇṭeṅkil}.)
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textquotedblleft{}If it rains, I will not come. If I get time tomorrow, I will call.\textquotedblright{}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}If you are coming, I will come too.\textquotedblright{}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}If he is at home, I will call. If there is time, let us go to a film.\textquotedblright{}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}Come quickly, otherwise the bus will go.\textquotedblright{}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}If you do not come, I will call.\textquotedblright{}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}It has rained since yesterday. If it rains tomorrow, I will not come.\textquotedblright{} — \emph{innale mutal maḻayāṇŭ. nāḷe maḻa peytāl ñān varilla.}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}If you want to go to Kerala, you must learn Malayalam.\textquotedblright{} — \emph{ninakkŭ kēraḷattil pōkaṇameṅkil nī malayāḷaṁ paṭhikkaṇaṁ.}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which ending waits for an event? (\textbf{-\ml{ആൽ}}, \emph{peytāl}.) Which checks a fact? (\textbf{-\ml{എങ്കിൽ}}, \emph{uṇṭeṅkil}.) \textquotedblleft{}Otherwise\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\ml{ഇല്ലെങ്കിൽ}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
